content.title: Open an existing published book detail page and inspect its bibliographic details, cover image, and package link
content.intent: Prove that a valid published-book detail page renders the promised credibility details, cover image, published-via package statement, and package link on the successful detail-page outcome.
content.technique_notes: Derived from REQ-08's successful detail-page outcome. Techniques: equivalence partitioning over resource state {existing published book}; happy-path inspection of a rendered web page. Kept as one scenario because the bibliographic fields, cover image, published-via statement, and package link are all promised on the same successful page outcome. No covering array applied: the source specifies no independent input dimensions to combine; the risk-judged interaction strength would have been 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss factor applies.

content.title: Use the publish-your-book CTA on a published book detail page to reach /publish
content.intent: Prove that the book-detail-page conversion CTA routes the reader from a valid book page into the publishing packages page.
content.technique_notes: Derived from REQ-08's routing promise for the detail-page CTA. Techniques: equivalence partitioning over resource state {existing published book}; happy-path navigation. Kept separate from the content-inspection scenario because activating the CTA changes the page outcome and proves a distinct propagation promise. No covering array applied: the source specifies no independent input dimensions to combine; the risk-judged interaction strength would have been 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss factor applies.

content.title: Request a published book detail page that does not exist and receive a 404
content.intent: Prove that a missing published-book detail request returns a 404 rather than rendering a misleading detail page.
content.technique_notes: Derived from REQ-08's explicit missing-resource behavior. Techniques: negative/error over resource state {nonexistent published book}. Kept separate because requesting a nonexistent book changes the outcome to an error page instead of a successful detail page. No covering array applied: the source specifies no independent input dimensions to combine; the risk-judged interaction strength would have been 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss factor applies.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Highest value because it covers the core reader-visible credibility content and the package attribution route on the successful detail-page outcome.
[value_score] High value because the CTA is the use-case's explicit conversion route from reader traffic back into publishing.

[value_score] High value negative coverage because the source explicitly promises 404 handling for missing books, but lower than the successful detail journey because it does not cover the page's primary credibility content.
